title: Chart transport of twisted sections to projective line
statement: For a field k, a coherent module G on polynomial Proj, and an integer n, after equipping its twisted global sections with the specified structure-map k-action, there exists a module L on the projective line over k, a k-linear equivalence from those sections to H⁰(L), and a proof that H⁰(L) is finite-dimensional over k.

proof.text: Polynomial Proj is locally Noetherian because its degree-zero ring is isomorphic to k and toSpecZero is locally of finite type. Apply the coherence criterion to G. The finite-pushforward theorem for the identity gives finite sections on every affine open. These modules are finitely presented over the Noetherian affine rings; apply the affine finite-presentation criterion and locality over the affine-open cover. This is the private, fully proved finitePresentation_of_coherent helper.

The degree-one variable opens cover polynomial Proj by iSup_basicOpen_eq_top'. Proj.isInvertible_twist gives invertibility of O(n) for every integer n. The proved source-library isFinitePresentation_tensorObj carries finite presentation of G to F = G tensor O(n); locally this tensor is isomorphic to G, including when n is negative or zero.

Define p as the canonical linearProjection for the two variables indexed by ULift(Fin 2). It is an isomorphism on each standard target chart by isIso_polynomial_linearProjection_restrict, hence globally by the Zariski locality of isomorphisms. Define L as pushforward p of F. An isomorphism is a closed immersion; the source-library closed-immersion theorem gives finite presentation of L, and the affine-pushforward theorem gives quasi-coherence.

Apply ProjectiveLine.finiteDimensional_H k L in degree zero. H.zeroLinearEquiv L identifies H-zero with global sections of L, which have the same underlying group as sections of F. linearProjection_over identifies p followed by the projective-line structure map with toSpecBase. Naturality of GammaSpecIso identifies the composite map on constants with rho, since algebraMap k A-zero is homogeneousSubmoduleZeroEquiv. Thus the H-zero equivalence is k-linear for exactly the prescribed action; take its inverse and pair it with finite dimensionality.

theorem serreTwistedSectionsTransport
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).Modules)
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent
      (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).toRingedSpace G)
    (n : ℤ) :
    let ρ := ((Proj.toSpecZero (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).appTop.hom.comp
      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).inv.hom).comp
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmoduleZeroEquiv (Fin 2) k).toRingHom
    letI := Module.compHom
      Γ(G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) n, ⊤) ρ
    ∃ (L : (ProjectiveLine (Spec (.of k))).Modules),
      Nonempty (Γ(G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) n, ⊤)
        ≃ₗ[k] L.H 0) ∧ FiniteDimensional k (L.H 0)
